colophon: Thus ends the Shiva Raksha Stotra, also called the Abhayankara Kavacha, spoken by Sri Yajnavalkya.

lines.1: Of this mantra, the Sri Shiva Raksha Stotra: the seer is Yajnavalkya;
lines.2: the deity is Sri Sadashiva; the meter is anushtubh;
lines.3: its use: recitation of the Shiva Raksha Stotra, for the pleasure of Sri Sadashiva.
lines.4: The story of the god of gods, Mahadeva, is purifying,
lines.5: boundless, supremely generous, the means to all four aims of life.
lines.6: Accompanied by Gauri and Vinayaka, five-faced, three-eyed,
lines.7: ten-armed: meditating thus on Shiva, let a person recite this Shiva-shield.
lines.8: May the bearer of the Ganga protect my head; he who wears the half-moon, my forehead;
lines.9: the destroyer of Kama, my eyes; he who is adorned with serpents, my ears.
lines.10: May the enemy of the triple city protect my nose; may the lord of the world protect my mouth;
lines.11: may the lord of speech protect my tongue; the dark-necked one, my neck.
lines.12: May Srikantha protect my throat; the bearer of the world's burden, my shoulders;
lines.13: the remover of the earth's burden, my arms; may the bearer of the Pinaka bow protect my hands.
lines.14: May Shankara protect my heart; the lord of Girija, my belly;
lines.15: may the conqueror of death protect my navel; he who wears the tiger skin, my hips.
lines.16: May he who loves the poor, the suffering, and all who come to him for shelter protect my haunches;
lines.17: may Maheshvara protect my thighs; the lord of the world, my knees.
lines.18: May the maker of the world protect my shins; the lord of the ganas, my ankles;
lines.19: the ocean of compassion, my feet; Sadashiva, all my limbs.
lines.20: The virtuous one who recites this shield, charged with Shiva's strength,
lines.21: will enjoy every desire and attain union with Shiva.
lines.22: Planets, ghosts, flesh-eaters and the rest, all who roam the three worlds,
lines.23: flee far and fast from one guarded by the name of Shiva.
lines.24: This armor of Parvati's lord, named Abhayankara, the Maker of Fearlessness:
lines.25: whoever wears it at the throat with devotion holds the three worlds in their power.
lines.26: Just as Narayana taught this Shiva-shield in a dream,
lines.27: so Yajnavalkya, prince of yogis, rising at dawn, wrote it down.
